One answer is: Yes. Physical properties can cause phenomenal properties, and phenomenal properties can cause physical properties.
A second answer is: Yes. Physical properties can cause phenomenal properties; but phenomenal properties cannot cause physical properties.
Ann reaches out for the apple and brings it to her mouth and takes a bite.
Ann feels hunger, and decides to walk to the fridge.
A third answer is: No. Physical and phenomenal properties cannot causally interact.
One reason for taking parallelism seriously is that causal connections between the physical and mental realms can look very puzzling.

There are two main lines of argument against the parellelist. This first is simple. It posits a massive coincidence between the physical and mental realms. On this view, mental events reliably correspond to physical events, but there are no causal connections at all between them. What could explain this?

For this reason, virtually all defenders of parallelism have been theists, who hold that God arranged the world so that there was a harmony between the physical and mental orders. But some have wondered whether God wasn’t thereby creating an illusion of causal connection between the mental and physical.
